title: add correlated-profile-snapshots and prose annotator for compact release snippets
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: onboarding churn and long, noisy changelogs make it hard for integrators to understand behavioral impact of new model variants. This PR introduces two complementary features: (1) correlated profile snapshots — a compact, sample-preserving snapshot format that records temporal baselines, representative probe samples, and profile correlation hashes; and (2) prose annotator — a lightweight, constrained natural-language composer that generates a 2-4 line human-reviewable release snippet describing key deltas (latency, throughput, accuracy markers, sample regressions) for use in automated release notes.

Summary of changes: implemented snapshot producer and consumer hooks, storage schema migration helpers, a small deterministic summarizer (prose annotator) with templates and safety clamps, and a reviewer workflow to accept/adjust generated snippets. The snapshot format is intentionally stable and content-addressed (profile-hash) so downstream tooling can reference specific baselines without large artifacts.

Design details: snapshot format groups probes into temporal buckets (recent/rolling-7/anchor) and keeps per-probe metadata: token distribution, seed-hash, probe-sig, and confidence bands. A correlation matrix (sparse) is emitted to help detect workload-preserving vs. semantic drift. The prose annotator uses rule-driven templates combined with a small transformer-based scorer (quantized) to pick candidate phrasing; all output goes through a lint step that enforces length, non-specificity of PII, and conservative normative language (avoid claims like "better" without metrics).

Migration: a migration utility converts existing profile records into the snapshot envelope; migration is opt-in per-namespace and runs as a background job with a throttled worker. Storage uses existing blobstore with a small index to map profile-hash -> snapshot metadata.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to the registry UI and onboarding API. Initially the prose annotator is enabled as "suggest" mode for 100% of internal model uploads and 20% of external uploads (canary by account label). After 2 weeks of feedback and fixes, it will be promoted to default suggestion for all onboard flows.

Testing and validation: unit tests for serializer/deserializer, end-to-end test that registers a snapshot and renders the suggested snippet, fuzz tests for snapshot ingestion, and a small manual review study (20 samples) to validate snippet usefulness.

Checklist:
- [x] snapshot schema, producer, and consumer
- [x] migration helper and background job scaffolding
- [x] prose annotator with template library and scorer
- [x] UI hook for reviewer to accept/edit snippet
- [x] telemetry (accept rate, edit rate, average snippet length)
- [x] docs + migration guide

Risks and mitigations: risk of overconfident prose or leaking training data; mitigated by strict template constraints, PII linter, and human-in-the-loop gating. Snapshot size growth mitigated by sample-preserving approach and retention policy (default 90 days, configurable).

review_conversation: Arjun Patel (reviewer): The correlation matrix looks useful, but I'm worried about size for large probe sets — can we make it sparse by default?
Maya Chen (author): Good call — implemented sparse encoding and added a compression knob. See commit c3d4e5f.
Li Wei (reviewer): The prose templates read well but sometimes imply improvements without numbers. Please add explicit metric placeholders or 'no significant change' fallback.
Maya Chen (author): Added fallback phrasing and enforced numeric placeholders where appropriate. Updated templates in prose_templates.py.
Riley Thompson (reviewer): We should ensure migration is opt-in for enterprise namespaces to avoid unexpected storage costs.
Maya Chen (author): Migration is opt-in and defaulted off for enterprise namespaces; clarified in migration docs and added a feature flag.
Arjun Patel (approver): LGTM after minor nits fixed. Approved.
merge_outcome: merged via squash, release: included in 2025-11-20 patch. Merge notes: squash commit contains snapshot schema, migration and prose annotator; all CI green.
release_notes: Introduce compact, correlated profile snapshots (temporal bucketing + sample-preserving probes) and an automated prose annotator that drafts concise release snippets for model onboardings. Migration helper included (opt-in). Adds reviewer UI and telemetry for suggestion acceptance. Default retention: 90 days.
notes_for_ops: Enable migration worker via helm flag registry.snapshotMigration.enabled=false by default. If enabling, monitor registry.blobstore.* metrics and ensure worker concurrency <= 4 for initial runs.
